text:
Anna Li: Acme CI reporting 401 invalid_api_key from our Go SDK when run in their containerized CI.
Kevin M.: any logs?
Anna Li: pasted log snippet:
```
Request: POST /v1/chat/completions
Authorization: Bearer "sk.d3Fz..."
Response 401 {"error":{"message":"invalid_api_key","type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```
Kevin M.: double-quotes around key — looks like their vault helper returns a JSON-encoded string or they used fmt.Sprintf("%q")
Anna Li: they confirmed their secret wrapper uses fmt.Sprintf("%q", secret) in Go. local dev gets raw secret, CI gets quoted string
eng-oncall: can you share minimal repro?
Anna Li: repro provided (sanitized):
```
# failing
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer \"$API_KEY\"" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3-small","prompt":"hi"}'

# working
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3-small","prompt":"hi"}'
```
Kevin M.: confirmed locally — header value must match token exactly; quotes break server validation
support-bot: created ticket SUP-2026-998 with repro + logs
Anna Li: customer workaround: strings.Trim(secret, `"`) before setting header in Go; they accepted workaround
eng-oncall: root cause = JSON quoting when fetching secret + header composition. Not SDK bug. Recommend KB and quick note in SDK FAQ
Kevin M.: I'll add a short DevEx blurb about fmt.Sprintf("%q") pitfalls and secret manager wrappers returning quoted JSON strings
Anna Li: will draft KB and ping @product for docs slot
eng-oncall: resolving thread — mark resolved after KB posted :white_check_mark:
